description:
Scholarship Overview

The Vice-Chancellor's PhD Scholarship (VCPS) at RMIT University is a fully funded scholarship awarded on the basis of academic excellence and research potential to local and international candidates undertaking a research doctoral degree. Funded by RMIT University, the VCPS provides comprehensive financial support including a generous stipend, research allowance, tuition fee offset, and relocation support. RMIT offers 10 VCPS awards each year.

Scholarship Benefits

  • Stipend of $48,299 per annum pro rata (full-time study) 2026 rate (indexation may apply yearly), representing an RMIT top-up of approximately $12,000 above the RTP rate.
  • Research support allowance of $5,000 per annum to support research activities.
  • International candidates also receive an RMIT Research International Tuition Fee Scholarship (RRITFS).
  • Local candidates (Australian and New Zealand citizens or permanent residents) receive an RTP Fee Offset scholarship, covering tuition fees for the maximum duration of candidature.
  • Relocation allowance of up to $515 per adult and $255 per child to a maximum of $1,540.
  • Paid sick, maternity, and parenting leave (within the limits of the Scholarship Terms and Conditions).
  • International candidates also receive Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for their visa duration.

Duration

Three and a half years full-time. This will be reduced by any periods of study undertaken towards an equivalent research degree prior to the commencement of the program at RMIT University.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for a VCPS scholarship you must hold, or be currently completing:

  • A Master by Research
  • A Master by Coursework with a significant research component graded as high distinction, or equivalent
  • An Honours degree achieving first-class Honours
  • A 4-year bachelor degree achieving a GPA of 4 or equivalent (80% or above)

If you do not hold one of the above qualifications, you will only be considered for scholarship if you have previous publications or significant research experience. All other applicants will be considered ineligible.

In addition, to be eligible for this scholarship you must:

  • Be an Australian Citizen, New Zealand Citizen or Permanent Resident of Australia, or an international candidate who is commencing in an RMIT PhD program from 1 January 2027
  • Have applied for a full-time PhD program at RMIT. Part-time VCPS may be approved for candidates with exceptional circumstances.

Ineligibility Criteria

You will be considered ineligible for a VCPS if:

  • You have already commenced your PhD program at RMIT
  • You already hold a research doctorate, or an equivalent research qualification
  • You are currently receiving another equivalent award, scholarship, or research-related salary providing a benefit greater than 75% of the RTP base rate
  • You have not met the English requirements by the published scholarship deadline (international only)

Application Process

  1. Follow the application process for a scholarship, including providing evidence of contact with the proposed supervisor.
  2. Complete the VCPS Expression of Interest form (student login required).
  3. Upload scanned (and where applicable, certified) copies of required documents: identification document, CV, academic transcripts, research proposal or project statement, English language proficiency evidence, SSVF Statement of Purpose (if required), certified copies, letter of financial guarantee (if sponsored).
  4. All scholarship applications must include evidence of contact with the proposed senior supervisor, uploaded as an additional document with your application.

All Outcomes FinalisedMarch 2027

Official Link

https://www.rmit.edu.au/scholarships/research/vcps

Important Notes

  • 10 VCPS awards offered each year.
  • VCPS scholarships are awarded based on a competitive selection process ranking applicants according to academic achievement, research outputs, and relevant professional experience.
  • Scholarship holders must commence studies in the scholarship commencement period in which they are applying and cannot defer to another year.
  • Part-time scholarships are not tax exempt.
  • For the Vice-Chancellor's PhD Scholarship (VCPS), the applicant must not have undertaken any prior higher degree by research candidature in the last three years.
